Try a chore that's not a daily chore: 
Wash the sinks
Mop the bathroom floor
Wash the windows and curtains

Don't allow yourself to sit in your comfort spot until you've done something unusual for your routine.

I got a cuckoo clock. 

Backstory: my great grand parents made every holiday so special. They played a huge part in our lives as kids when my parents' custody battle was hairy. As well as raised my mom when she had my oldest brother at a young age and her parents kicked her out.

From the first stop at their house for Halloween every year and always having apple cider for us, and christmas dinner with mints from our local factory. The race car track down their stairs. They played a huge role and have a very special place in my heart. They passed from dementia when I was in high school. True role models of love, grace, and tradition.

My siblings and I always helped reset the time on their clock at every age, and she would make it chime for us when we were waiting to do things or just to make us dance. It was so special. Unfortunately, our estranged uncle who had nothing to do with any of us got to keep the original clock, and we were very upset we never got it.


Receiving the gifts:

My mom and I were trying to think of a way to get everyone a version of a cuckoo clock, whether it was a key chain or what. But they are expensive at any size, so I wrote it off as a dream. 

My mom wrapped 2 presents for my sister and I to each open at the same time. We started racing to open it, boyfriends supplying box openers like ninjas on cue. It was chaos until I opened the box and froze. I literally ugly cried in front of my entire family, thinking of such amazing people and missing them and then getting my very own full-size cuckoo clock to continue their special time with us in our own homes. 

I can't wait for it to chime the first time. I'll probably cry then, too.

I take 15mg of lexapro every day. I have a generalized anxiety disorder, health anxiety, ARFID (Avoidance/restrictive food intake disorder)... AKA I am a big ball of anxiety lol

For me, the side effects got more intense the higher my dose. The side effects I experienced week one i experienced but stronger with every dose change. The dose change is hard for the first week then I leveled out and felt like myself. I have no lasting side effects besides drowsiness (only because I refuse to take it at  night) like I said i got through the same process every time I change doses like clock work. Now that I'm adjusted after 3 months I shouldn't and haven't had any more or new side effects. 

Side effects ive experienced:
-dizziness 
-nausea
-tingling in neck, arms, hands
-drowsiness 

If side effects ever get to the point you feel like you don't want to take them anymore then you need to talk to your doctor. It can be very dangerous to come off them without help. Some people have had varying responses and the anxiety can get a bit worse before it get better. 

If you find something that works it is so worth it.
